The goal of this notebook is to quantify jointly the impact of large dams and
water quality on food web structure. It follows the structure of
[D13](D13-dam-impact-foodweb.qmd), which did it for dams only, and adds the
water quality index of [D14](D14-nutrient-impact-presence.qmd). To do so, we

- keep the food webs of D13 at the visits with a predicted water quality
- model the impact of dams and water quality on the descriptors of food web
  structure, together in the same model
- check whether the dam effects of D13 hold once water quality is accounted for
- investigate how the impacts of the two stressors are mediated by species.

Following D14, we keep the two stressors additive: their interaction on species
presence was weak and inconsistent across species.

## Setup

```{r setup}
library(renv)
renv::load()
library(targets)
library(here)
tar_config_set(
  store = here::here("_targets")
)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
devtools::load_all()
nice_theme()
```

## Food webs and water quality

### Data

We use the observed food webs of D13 and their descriptors, at the visits whose
site is a NAIADES station, with the water quality index (PC1 of D14) predicted
in the visit year. Water quality is centred and scaled over these visits, so
its effects are per standard deviation; higher values mean better water quality
(less nutrients, more oxygen). The two axes of the PCA of the descriptors of
D13 are kept: PC1, the simplicity axis, and PC2, the richness to
top-heaviness gradient. To avoid confusion with the water quality index, we
call these axes "Structure PC1" and "Structure PC2".

```{r webs}
metric_label <- c(
  fish_richness = "Fish richness",
  mean_trophic_level = "Mean trophic level",
  fish_diet_overlap = "Fish diet overlap",
  trophic_redundancy = "Trophic redundancy",
  log_biomass = "Total biomass (log)",
  biomass_trophic_level = "Mean trophic level (biomass)",
  biomass_pyramid = "Biomass-trophic level correlation",
  PC1 = "Structure PC1 (simplicity)",
  PC2 = "Structure PC2 (richness to top-heaviness)"
)
web <- tar_read(quality_foodweb)
tibble(
  webs = c("D13", "with water quality"),
  visits = c(nrow(tar_read(dam_foodweb)), nrow(web)),
  sites = c(n_distinct(tar_read(dam_foodweb)$site), n_distinct(web$site))
) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

### Dams and water quality

If dams and water quality were strongly correlated, their effects could not be
separated. We plot the water quality of the visits against their dam
accumulation.

```{r quality-dam}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.5

ggplot(web, aes(accumulation, quality)) +
  geom_bin_2d(bins = 30) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#B2182B", linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Blues", direction = 1, transform = "log10") +
  labs(x = "log(1 + dams)", y = "Water quality (scaled)", fill = "Visits")
```

```{r quality-dam-correlation}
tibble(
  `Spearman correlation` = cor(web$accumulation, web$quality, method = "spearman")
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

Next, the Spearman correlation of water quality with each descriptor, before
any control.

```{r quality-metric-correlation}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4

tibble(
  metric = names(metric_label),
  rho = purrr::map_dbl(metric, \(m) cor(web[[m]], web$quality, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"))
) |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric_label[metric], rev(metric_label))) |>
  ggplot(aes(rho, metric)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = rho, yend = metric), color = "#2166AC", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(color = "#2166AC", size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Spearman correlation with water quality", y = NULL)
```

## Model dam and water quality impacts on food web structure

Each descriptor is modelled as in D13 (position controls, sampling effort, site
and year effects, spatial field; Poisson for fish richness, Gaussian otherwise),
with dam accumulation and water quality in the same model. Each model is fitted
without and with log richness as a control, to see whether the effects pass
through the number of species only.

```{r structure-models}
setting <- tar_read(quality_structure_setting)
metric_sd <- web |>
  summarise(across(all_of(names(metric_label)), \(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "metric", values_to = "sd")
structure_effect <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(setting)), \(i) {
  tar_read(quality_structure_model)[[i]]$summary.fixed |>
    as_tibble(rownames = "term") |>
    filter(term %in% c("accumulation", "quality")) |>
    transmute(
      metric = setting$metric[i], model = setting$model[i],
      control = if_else(setting$richness[i], "with richness", "without richness"),
      term, mean, lower = `0.045quant`, upper = `0.955quant`
    )
}) |>
  left_join(metric_sd, by = "metric") |>
  # Gaussian metrics on the sd scale, to compare them; richness stays on the
  # log scale.
  mutate(across(c(mean, lower, upper), \(x) if_else(metric == "fish_richness", x, x / sd)))
stressor_label <- c(accumulation = "Dam accumulation", quality = "Water quality")
```

Effects of the two stressors in the joint model: dam effect per unit of
$\log(1 + \text{dams})$, water quality effect per standard deviation; Gaussian
descriptors in standard deviations, fish richness on the log scale.

```{r structure-effect-plot}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

structure_effect |>
  filter(model == "additive") |>
  mutate(
    metric = factor(metric_label[metric], rev(metric_label)),
    term = factor(stressor_label[term], stressor_label)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(mean, metric, color = control)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
  geom_pointrange(
    aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper),
    position = position_dodge(0.5), size = 0.3
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`without richness` = "grey40", `with richness` = "#2166AC")) +
  facet_wrap(~term, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Effect (91% CI)", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

**Results:** dams and water quality act on different parts of the web.
Better water quality shifts the biomass up the web (biomass-weighted trophic
level +0.15 sd and biomass-trophic level correlation +0.19 sd per sd of water
quality), with slightly fewer species (about -4% per sd) and less total
biomass. It moves the webs along Structure PC2, towards species-poor and
top-heavy webs, but not along Structure PC1. Dams, as in D13, simplify the webs
(Structure PC1 +0.20): fewer species, less biomass, lower in the web and more
redundant. The water quality effects hold at equal richness, so they do not
only come from the number of species.

### Do the dam effects hold with water quality?

Dam effect in the model with dams only (as in D13, on the visits of this
notebook) and in the joint model, without richness control.

```{r dam-effect-comparison}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5

structure_effect |>
  filter(term == "accumulation", control == "without richness") |>
  mutate(
    metric = factor(metric_label[metric], rev(metric_label)),
    model = factor(model, c("dam", "additive"), c("dams only", "dams + water quality"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(mean, metric, color = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
  geom_pointrange(
    aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper),
    position = position_dodge(0.5), size = 0.3
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`dams only` = "grey40", `dams + water quality` = "#2166AC")) +
  labs(x = "Effect of log(1 + dams) (91% CI)", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

**Results:** the dam effects barely change when water quality is added, so
the D13 results are not driven by water quality. The only change is on
Structure PC2, where the dam effect becomes weakly negative (-0.11, 91% CI
-0.21 to -0.00).

## How species mediate the impacts on food web structure

As in D13, we ask which species mediate the effects on food web structure,
summarised by Structure PC1, now for both stressors. The contribution of species
$s$ to the effect of a stressor on Structure PC1 is
$$
\beta_s \, \overline{p_s (1 - p_s)} \, (-r_s),
$$
with $\beta_s$ the effect of the stressor on the presence of $s$ (logit scale),
from the presence model of D14 with dams and water quality (additive, with
spatial field), $p_s$ its fitted presence probability, and $r_s$ the change of
Structure PC1 when $s$ is removed from the webs (from D13). The expected effect
is the sum over the species. The uncertainty of $\beta_s$ and $r_s$ is
propagated by drawing both, and the null model shuffles the effects $\beta_s$
among the species.

```{r species-mediation}
mediation_stressor <- tar_read(mediation_stressor)
stressor_name <- c(accumulation = "accumulation", PC1 = "quality") # Term in the structure models.
decomposition <- setNames(tar_read(stressor_decomposition), mediation_stressor)
permutation <- setNames(tar_read(stressor_permutation), mediation_stressor)
removal_effect <- tar_read(species_removal_effect) |>
  filter(metric == "PC1") |>
  select(species, importance = mean, importance_lower = lower, importance_upper = upper)
species_mediation <- purrr::imap_dfr(decomposition, \(d, stressor) {
  d$species |>
    filter(metric == "PC1") |>
    left_join(removal_effect, by = "species") |>
    mutate(stressor = stressor_name[stressor])
})
```

Effect of each stressor on Structure PC1 estimated by the joint model, predicted
from the change of species presence, and predicted from the same changes
shuffled among species, without and at equal richness (see D13).

```{r species-mediation-total}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.8

estimate_level <- c(
  "Estimated by the model", "Predicted from species presence", "Null (shuffled effects)"
)
metric_control <- c(PC1 = "without richness", PC1_richness = "with richness")
bind_rows(
  structure_effect |>
    filter(metric == "PC1", model == "additive") |>
    transmute(stressor = term, estimate = estimate_level[1], control, mean, lower, upper),
  purrr::map_dfr(mediation_stressor, \(stressor) bind_rows(
    decomposition[[stressor]]$draw |> mutate(estimate = estimate_level[2]),
    permutation[[stressor]] |> mutate(estimate = estimate_level[3])
  ) |>
    summarise(
      mean = mean(change), lower = quantile(change, 0.045), upper = quantile(change, 0.955),
      .by = c(metric, estimate)
    ) |>
    transmute(stressor = stressor_name[stressor], estimate, control = metric_control[metric], mean, lower, upper))
) |>
  mutate(
    estimate = factor(estimate, rev(estimate_level)),
    stressor = factor(stressor_label[stressor], stressor_label)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(mean, estimate, color = control)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
  geom_pointrange(
    aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper),
    position = position_dodge(0.5), size = 0.3
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`without richness` = "grey40", `with richness` = "#2166AC")) +
  facet_wrap(~stressor, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Effect on Structure PC1 (sd of PC1)", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

**Results:** for dams, D13 holds: the effect predicted from the change of
species presence (0.14) is close to the model estimate (0.20) and larger than
the null (0.06), so dams hit the species that matter for the structure. For
water quality, both the model estimate and the predicted effect on Structure
PC1 are close to zero (predicted -0.01, 91% CI -0.03 to 0.01): water quality
changes species presence, but these changes cancel out on Structure PC1.

Decomposition of the predicted effect at the species level, for the 15 species
with the strongest mediated effect of each stressor.

```{r species-mediation-plot}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
#| layout-ncol: 1

species_step <- c(
  importance = "Contribution to Structure PC1",
  presence = "Impact on presence",
  contribution = "Effect mediated by the species"
)
plot_mediation <- function(mediation, title) {
  bind_rows(
    mediation |> transmute(species, step = "importance", mean = importance, lower = importance_lower, upper = importance_upper),
    mediation |> transmute(species, step = "presence", mean = presence, lower = presence_lower, upper = presence_upper),
    mediation |> transmute(species, step = "contribution", mean = contribution, lower, upper)
  ) |>
    semi_join(slice_max(mediation, abs(contribution), n = 15), by = "species") |>
    mutate(
      step = factor(species_step[step], species_step),
      species = factor(species, arrange(mediation, contribution)$species)
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(mean, species)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
    geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), size = 0.3, color = "#2166AC") +
    facet_wrap(~step, scales = "free_x") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = title) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"))
}
species_mediation |>
  split(~stressor) |>
  purrr::iwalk(\(mediation, stressor) print(plot_mediation(mediation, stressor_label[stressor])))
```

**Results:** the eel still mediates most of the dam effect. Better water
quality favours the brown trout and the sculpin, whose presence makes webs less
simple, but disfavours piscivores and tolerant species (eel, pike, pikeperch,
perch, pumpkinseed, black bullhead), whose presence also makes webs less
simple. The two groups balance out on Structure PC1.

To separate the number of species lost from their identity, we split the
predicted dam effect as in D13. We do not split the effect of water quality:
its predicted effect is close to zero, so shares of it are meaningless. With
$a_s = \beta_s \overline{p_s (1 - p_s)}$ the change of presence of species $s$,
and $\bar{a}$ its mean over the species,
$$
\Delta = \bar{a} \sum_s (-r_s) + \sum_s (a_s - \bar{a}) (-r_s).
$$
The first term is the effect if dams hit all species equally (the number of
species lost), the second the effect of dams hitting some species more than
others (which species are lost). The bars below the top one split the second
part by species.

```{r species-mediation-split}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| layout-ncol: 1

plot_split <- function(mediation, title) {
  mean_presence <- mean(mediation$presence)
  species_identity <- mediation |>
    transmute(item = species, value = (presence - mean_presence) * -importance) |>
    arrange(desc(abs(value)))
  n_shown <- 6
  species_identity <- bind_rows(
    head(species_identity, n_shown),
    tibble(
      item = paste0("Other species (", nrow(species_identity) - n_shown, ")"),
      value = sum(species_identity$value[-seq_len(n_shown)])
    )
  )
  number_part <- mean_presence * sum(-mediation$importance)
  total <- number_part + sum(species_identity$value)
  # Parts in percentage of the predicted effect.
  number_part <- 100 * number_part / total
  species_identity <- mutate(species_identity, value = 100 * value / total)
  split_part <- bind_rows(
    tibble(
      item = "Predicted effect",
      part = c("Number of species lost", "Which species are lost"),
      start = c(0, number_part), end = c(number_part, 100)
    ),
    species_identity |>
      mutate(
        end = number_part + cumsum(value), start = lag(end, default = number_part),
        part = "Which species are lost"
      )
  ) |>
    mutate(position = match(item, unique(item)), value = end - start)
  ggplot(split_part) +
    geom_rect(
      aes(xmin = pmin(start, end), xmax = pmax(start, end),
          ymin = position - 0.4, ymax = position + 0.4, fill = part)
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(x = (start + end) / 2, y = position, label = sprintf("%.0f%%", value)),
      data = filter(split_part, position == 1), color = "white", size = 3.2
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(x = pmax(start, end), y = position, label = sprintf("%+.0f%%", value)),
      data = filter(split_part, position > 1), hjust = -0.15, color = "grey20", size = 3
    ) +
    scale_y_reverse(breaks = unique(split_part$position), labels = unique(split_part$item)) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.08))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Number of species lost` = "grey60", `Which species are lost` = "#2166AC")) +
    labs(x = "Share of the predicted dam effect on Structure PC1 (%)", y = NULL, fill = NULL, title = title) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}
plot_split(filter(species_mediation, stressor == "accumulation"), stressor_label["accumulation"])
```

**Results:** as in D13, about half of the predicted dam effect (56%) comes
from the number of species lost, and the rest mostly from the eel being hit
harder than the other species.

## Conclusion

- Dams and water quality are only moderately correlated at the fish visits,
  and the dam effects of D13 hold once water quality is accounted for.
- The two stressors act on different dimensions of the webs. Dams simplify
  them (Structure PC1), mostly through the loss of the eel. Water quality
  shifts them along Structure PC2: where the water is clean, webs hold fewer
  species and more of their biomass high in the web.
- On Structure PC1, the effects of water quality on species presence cancel
  out: sensitive species (trout, sculpin) and tolerant piscivores replace each
  other.

*To discuss:* the mediation is done on Structure PC1 only, as in D13; since
water quality acts on Structure PC2, the same analysis on PC2 would tell which
species carry its effect. The removal effects $r_s$ come from all the D13 webs,
not only those with water quality, and the uncertainty of the predicted water
quality is not propagated.
